newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian coalition to decide on oil prices on July 2.
newsitem.headline: Indian coalition to decide on oil prices on July 2.

text.p: India's ruling United Front coalition will decide whether to raise petroleum prices at a meeting on July 2, Information and Broadcasting Minister Jaipal Reddy said on Thursday.

"On July 2, we will take a final decision. How tough the decision will be, I don't know," Reddy, who is also the spokesman of the 15-party centre-left coalition, told the Foreign Correspondents' Club in the capital.

At its last meeting on June 16, Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's coalition deferred a decision on whether to raise prices to plug the government's mounting debt to state oil companies, estimated at 155 billion rupees ($4.3 billion) at the end of March.

This week the alliance, deeply divided over the issue, postponed a meeting set for Friday until July 2. Gujral and Finance Minister P. Chidambaram favour raising the prices of some petroleum prices, but they are strongly opposed by leftwing parties in the coalition.

Reddy said the two-month-old government would survive corruption charges against the leader of Gujral's Janata Dal party. "Whatever the outcome of the crisis, it will have no effect on the quality or continuance of the government," he said.
"This government will last much longer than many fear or hope," Reddy said.
